hypothesis: One CPU pass over a separate 9,746,875-bit training trace may produce a better compact final bit predictor than the prior screen-trained one-pass checkpoint, without fitting the screen repeatedly.
selection: Train each rate once from the original shipped BF16 checkpoint on the separate four-megabyte range. Export each to the same 7,386-byte BF16 format. Select the lowest frozen screen probability cost, breaking ties by lower rate. Require at least one byte improvement against the prior screen-trained checkpoint, then check that one selected model once on the disjoint fixture with the same one-byte gate.
promotion: Only a model passing both frozen replay-cost gates may enter real archive trials. Reused fixtures and probability costs are not full release or prize scores. Preserve all failures and do not retune after the holdout result.
raw_trace_storage: Approximately 940 MB of original trace/channel/probability data stay local; commit bounded reports, logs, hashes and selected compact weights only.
